card.name: Paso Doble
card.tagline: Spain — the bullfight rendered as dance. He is the matador, she is the cape.
card.profile: Pasodoble is the Spanish bullfight dance — the lead steps as the matador, the follower flowing like the muleta cape, the rhythm a driving 2/4 march. Originated in late-18th-century Spanish military marches and codified into a competitive ballroom form in the early 20th century, pasodoble is the most theatrical of the five International Latin dances. The most iconic pasodoble tune — 'España Cañí' — opens every Spanish bullfight to this day.
card.insight: It was composed in 1957, with lyrics by Guillermo González Ospina and music by Juan Mari Asins inspired by the Spanish classic "España cañí". These dances, developed around 1538, were a gradual combination of Castillian music and dance with the "garrotín", a fast and repetitive Romani couples dance, adapted into a march form.
